solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ancient Greek marble finally succeeded in America

indicators.note: in places the preceding pair of letters inside the phrase for the country

parts.note: America is often called the US

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the closing letter of marble
S is the abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: A classical marble sculpture ends up sold to an American buyer.
explanation.walkthrough: The ES pair goes inside THE US, splitting it after THE. The surface also nods to the reclining 'Theseus' among the Elgin Marbles.
explanation.definitionFit: Theseus is the legendary hero of ancient Athens who slew the Minotaur, so he is a Greek of antiquity.

clue.text: Rising price accepted in lots for very large fish

indicators.note: in places the reversed pair inside the word for lots

parts.note: tons of something means lots of it

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the letters read upwards, back to front

parts.note: pr. abbreviates price
A is the commercial abbreviation for accepted, as on a bill

explanation.surface: Prices climb as big fish are bought at auction in lots.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarpons are huge silvery game fish of the Atlantic, often well over six feet long.

clue.text: Not in good condition after start of home care

indicators.note: start of means the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the opening letter of home
out can mean unwell or out of order, not in shape

explanation.surface: Someone ailing comes out of hospital into home care.
explanation.walkthrough: Care is the noun as in 'not give a hoot'; hout is a variant spelling of that hoot.
explanation.definitionFit: A hout, like a hoot, is the tiny amount of concern in phrases such as not caring two hoots.

clue.text: Trouble over a nude shot

indicators.note: shot means broken or ruined, so the letters before it are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fuss arose about a nude photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble' looks like a verb opening the wordplay and 'shot' like a photograph; in fact 'Trouble' is the definition and 'shot' means wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: To take trouble over something is to make an effort, and an endeavour is exactly such an earnest effort.

clue.text: Went around one part of hospital holding doctor up

indicators.note: holding means the department wraps round the other word

parts.note: ENT, ear nose and throat, is a hospital department

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: to doctor results is to rig them

explanation.surface: A consultant did a round of one hospital ward, propping up a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a medic, apt in a hospital; it is the verb meaning to falsify.
explanation.definitionFit: Engirt is the past form of engird, to encircle, so it means surrounded or went around.

clue.text: Middle East ruler brought about government broadcast with a shock

indicators.note: brought about means the ruler is placed around the letter

parts.note: a shah was the ruler of Iran
G abbreviates government
a programme broadcast has been aired

explanation.surface: A Middle Eastern ruler ordered a government broadcast that came as a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: A shock is a thick mass of hair, not a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Shag-haired describes a person with rough, shaggy hair, that is with a shock of hair.

clue.text: Soak clothing with difficulty in tiny stream

indicators.note: clothing means dressing round, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: to ret flax is to soak it
ill can mean badly or hardly, as in 'ill afford'

explanation.surface: Getting clothes wet with difficulty in a trickling brook.
explanation.definitionFit: A rillet is a little rill, and a rill is a small brook, so it is a very small watercourse.

clue.text: Piece of music taken from a light part of raga?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: taken from means one piece is removed out of the following words

parts.note: a lamp gives light
a piece, the opening letter, of music

explanation.surface: A short instrumental passage lifted from a gentle section of an Indian raga.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of music' looks like the definition, but it supplies only the M that leaves A LAMP; the definition is at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The alap is the slow, unaccompanied opening section of a raga performance in Indian classical music.

clue.text: Oriental massaging offered by Korean model?

indicators.note: offered by means supplied from within the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: An Eastern massage is advertised by a Korean model.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is set within the fodder's own scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Anmo is the traditional Chinese and Japanese massage technique, an Eastern form of manipulating the body.

clue.text: Star partner of Sonny in a number about right

indicators.note: in puts the singer inside the string that follows

parts.note: taken as written
N stands for a number in algebra
a. abbreviates about, from Latin ante or circa usage
R abbreviates right
Cher sang with Sonny Bono as Sonny and Cher

explanation.surface: Sonny's famous partner stars in a song about getting things right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' looks like a description of Cher; it is an actual star. CHER goes in after the first A of A-N-A-R.
explanation.definitionFit: Achernar is the brightest star in the constellation Eridanus, one of the brightest in the night sky.

clue.text: Purse empty, urgent call for funds in Latin America

indicators.note: empty means the inside is removed, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: the outside letters of purse
SOS is the distress signal

explanation.surface: With an empty purse, someone sends an urgent appeal for money in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: The peso is the currency unit of many Latin American countries, such as Mexico and Argentina.

clue.text: In a risky situation having a cracking future?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in a precarious position
second meaning, literal and playful: standing where the surface below may soon crack

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracking' sounds like praise for an excellent future; read literally, a skater on a frozen pond is about to hear it crack.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in a precarious position, from the literal danger of standing where frozen water is weak.

clue.text: Pole mentioned being unskilled

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken out, so the sound of the word counts, not its spelling

parts.note: a rood is a pole or rod, also an old measure of length

explanation.surface: A Polish worker is said to be untrained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' with its capital looks like a nationality; it is a rod, a rood.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude in an older sense means primitive or roughly made, so lacking skill or refinement.

clue.text: Chef's papers from past, many in stacks

parts.note: pa. abbreviates past, as in pa. t. for past tense

indicators.note: in places the word for many inside the word for stacks

parts.note: stacks are piles
a lot means many

explanation.surface: A cook's old documents come from the past, many kept in heaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Papers' suggests documents; these are paper frills and wrappers used in cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Papillotes are the greased paper cases in which food is baked, or frills on cutlet bones, so a cook's papers.

clue.text: Egyptian girls pretended indeed to get backing

indicators.note: getting backing means the whole run of letters is read from the back

parts.note: sham as a verb means to pretend
la is an archaic exclamation meaning indeed

explanation.surface: Some Egyptian girls faked it convincingly to win support.
explanation.definitionFit: Almahs were professional dancing and singing girls of Egypt, so the plural fits girls from that country.

clue.text: Publicity rebuffed after private meetings exposed in the theatre

parts.note: Pte is the army abbreviation for a private soldier

indicators.note: rebuffed suggests being pushed back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to give something air is to publicise it

explanation.surface: Publicity was turned down after some discreet backstage meetings at the playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre is the operating theatre: a pterion is where skull bones meet, seen when the head is opened in surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: A pterion is the junction point of four skull bones, so the plural names bone meetings a surgeon may see.

clue.text: Comparatively weak on the road? Not this ruler

parts.note: tamer means milder, less fierce
a lane is a road

explanation.surface: A slower driver is told to keep off the road, unlike this mighty conqueror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not this' is a wry aside: the wordplay calls him tamer, but the ruler was famously ferocious.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamerlane, or Timur, was the fourteenth-century Turco-Mongol conqueror who ruled a vast Central Asian empire.

clue.text: Wrap up duck rolls and fish

indicators.note: something that rolls over turns end to end, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: hap is a dialect word meaning to wrap up or cover
a duck is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: A cook wraps the duck, rolls it up and serves it with fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The opah, or moonfish, is a large brightly coloured ocean species.

clue.text: Coward's Private Lives primarily about love, romantic or not?

indicators.note: about means the pair of letters goes around the next one
primarily points to the opening letters of the words before it

parts.note: the opening letters of the two words
love is zero in tennis, O

indicators.note: romantic suggests fanciful and wild, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Noël Coward's play Private Lives is about love, but is it romantic?
explanation.walkthrough: Coward is the playwright of Private Lives, but here it is the definition: a coward.
explanation.definitionFit: A poltroon is an utter coward, an old word for a spiritless person.

clue.text: Tries to contain pressure for sulphides?

indicators.note: to contain means the following letter is held inside the word

parts.note: a judge hears, that is tries, a case
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to keep the pressure contained when dealing with sulphur compounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tries' reads as attempts; here it is the courtroom sense, as a judge does.
explanation.definitionFit: Hepar, or liver of sulphur, is an old chemistry name for liver-coloured sulphide compounds.

clue.text: Small number spoil quarters for religious trainees

parts.note: No. is the short form of number
to vitiate is to spoil or impair

explanation.surface: A few people ruin the living accommodation of trainee monks.
explanation.definitionFit: A novitiate is the house or wing of a religious order where novices live during probation.

clue.text: A bit of cloth advanced by the French?

definitions.text: A bit of cloth advanced by the French

parts.note: per means a, as in so much per day

indicators.note: a bit of a word is its opening letter here

parts.note: the opening letter of cloth
A abbreviates advanced
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A fabric introduced to us by the French.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: the cloth was introduced from France, as its French-looking name suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Percale is a closely woven cotton fabric used for bed linen, a word that came into English from French.

clue.text: Lime flourishing with one old group of trees

indicators.note: flourishing suggests growth and waving about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
an ace is a one on dice or cards
ae. abbreviates aetatis, aged

explanation.surface: A lime tree thriving beside an ancient one forms a grove.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'lime' looks like a member of the group, but the answer is the mahogany family, not the lime family.
explanation.definitionFit: Meliaceae is the botanical family name of mahogany and its relatives, a taxonomic group of mostly trees.

clue.text: Sort of dog some like unrestrained for a change

indicators.note: for a change means the letters are altered in order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: unrestrained means freed of its restraints, the outer letters, keeping the middle

parts.note: the inner letters of like

explanation.surface: Some people like a dog to be let off the leash for a change.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eskimo dog is a breed of sled dog, also called the Canadian Inuit dog.

clue.text: Language? Yes, used by many Andeans raising alpacas, originally

parts.note: ay is an old or dialect form of yes

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letters of the words before it

parts.note: the opening letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A speaker asks if the tongue really is spoken by many Andean alpaca herders.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is true to life: the answer is spoken in the Andes.
explanation.definitionFit: Aymara is an indigenous tongue spoken by about two million people in Bolivia and Peru.

clue.text: Sheet of ratings shocks lecturer

parts.note: to stun is to shock
L is a standard abbreviation for lecturer

explanation.surface: A table of grades startles a university teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheet of ratings' suggests a list of scores; ratings are ordinary sailors, and a sheet here is a sail.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuns'l is the sailors' contraction of studding sail, an extra sail rigged out from a square sail.

clue.text: Almost convinced about old Italian bread

indicators.note: almost means falling just short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to be sold on an idea is to be convinced about it

explanation.surface: Someone is nearly persuaded about a vintage Italian loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: Bread is slang for money, not a loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: The soldo was a former Italian copper coin, and bread is slang for cash.

clue.text: Exclamation from Britain with extremes of bitter winter weather?

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for Britain

indicators.note: extremes here are the ends of each word, the closing letter of each

parts.note: the closing letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A shivering Briton cries out in a bitter winter.
explanation.definitionFit: Brrr is the interjection people use to show they are shivering with cold.

clue.text: Peculiar contracted fence of stakes catching fish

indicators.note: contracted means shortened, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: weird means peculiar

explanation.surface: An odd shrunken fence of stakes manages to trap fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A weir, besides a river dam, is a fish trap made of stakes set in a stream.

clue.text: Day off, climbed high in a tree

indicators.note: high as in intoxicated, so the letters are muddled
off means that letter is taken away from the word

parts.note: D abbreviates day
taken as written

explanation.surface: On a day off, someone climbed high up a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The emblic is the Indian gooseberry or myrobalan, a tree grown for its sour fruit.

clue.text: Russian in assembly dead detached?

indicators.note: detached means cut off, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a divan is a council or assembly in the Middle East
D abbreviates dead

explanation.surface: Was a Russian in the parliament left aloof and lifeless?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assembly' suggests putting something together; it is a council, a divan.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan is the stock typical Russian name, used for any Russian man or soldier.

clue.text: Miss and one with a Tesla have a breakdown

parts.note: to miss out on a chance means failing to keep it
I is the Roman numeral one
T is the symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density

explanation.surface: A young woman and a Tesla driver both suffer a car breakdown.
explanation.walkthrough: Tesla looks like the car; it is the physics unit.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose it is the informal idiom for losing self-control, going to pieces emotionally.

clue.text: Griddle in pub not half advanced

indicators.note: not half means half of the word is dropped, keeping the front half

parts.note: a tavern is a pub
A abbreviates advanced

explanation.surface: The cooking plate at the pub has barely moved forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A tava is a flat griddle pan used in South Asian cooking for flatbreads.

clue.text: Three notes go with x-ray measurement

parts.note: do, si and me are three tonic sol-fa notes
to have a go is to have a try

explanation.surface: Three musical notes are paired with an x-ray reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Dosimetry is measuring the radiation dose a body receives, as from x-rays.

clue.text: A certain Republican's whopper

parts.note: a certain person is 'one' in phrases like one Mr Smith
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A particular Republican politician has told a big lie.
explanation.definitionFit: A oner is something outstanding or exceptional of its kind, as a whopper is something huge.

clue.text: Fleshy part of leg cut in wound seen on a muscle

indicators.note: in puts the shortened word inside the other letters
wound as in twisted round, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: cut means the word loses its tail letter

parts.note: the calf is the fleshy back of the lower leg

explanation.surface: A cut to the calf has caused a wound seen on a muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' reads as an injury, apt beside a cut leg, but it is the past tense of wind.
explanation.definitionFit: The scalenes are a set of muscles in the side of the neck, named for their uneven triangular shape.
